label: Classification of Symplectic Toric Manifolds
notes: Welcome to Lecture 28, spanning printed pages 175 to 180. Today we close the loop on Hamiltonian torus actions by stating the Delzant theorem: a compact symplectic toric manifold is determined, up to equivariant symplectomorphism, by a single combinatorial object, its moment polytope. Geometry becomes the bookkeeping of a labeled polytope.

label: What Is a Symplectic Toric Manifold
notes: Fix the objects we classify. A symplectic toric manifold is a compact connected symplectic manifold of dimension twice n, carrying an effective Hamiltonian action of the n-torus with a moment map. Effectiveness and the half-dimensional torus are exactly what make the action rigid enough to be encoded combinatorially without losing information.

label: The Moment Image Is a Polytope
notes: By the Atiyah and Guillemin-Sternberg convexity theorem, the moment map image of a compact connected Hamiltonian torus space is a convex polytope, the convex hull of the images of the fixed points. For toric manifolds this polytope lives in the dual of the torus Lie algebra and carries all the data we need.

label: Delzant Polytopes: Three Conditions
notes: Not every polytope arises. A Delzant polytope satisfies three local conditions at every vertex: simplicity, meaning exactly n edges meet there; rationality, meaning those edge directions are lattice vectors; and smoothness, meaning the primitive edge vectors form a basis of the integer lattice. These tests are independent and entirely local.

label: Smoothness as Unimodularity
notes: Smoothness is the subtle condition, so make it concrete. At each vertex the n primitive edge vectors must span the full integer lattice, equivalently their matrix has determinant plus or minus one. In the plane this is the determinant test on adjacent primitive normals. The right-hand corner with edge slope two fails: its determinant is two.

label: Half-Space Description
notes: The construction never starts from a drawn polygon; it starts from data. Write the polytope as an intersection of half-spaces, one primitive outward normal vector and one real constant per facet. For the standard simplex the three inequalities x one at least zero, x two at least zero, and their sum at most one give the normals minus e one, minus e two, and one one.

label: The Delzant Theorem
notes: Here is the classification. The map sending a symplectic toric manifold to its moment image is a bijection onto Delzant polytopes, with equivariant symplectomorphisms on the left and lattice-preserving translations on the right. Two toric manifolds are equivalent exactly when their polytopes agree up to translation. Combinatorics fully captures the symplectic geometry.

label: From Polytope to Manifold
notes: Surjectivity is proved by an explicit construction, detailed next lecture. The d facet normals define a map pi from R to the d-th power onto R to the n-th, sending each basis vector to a normal. Its kernel exponentiates to a subtorus N of the standard d-torus, and reducing the model space C to the d at level zero builds the manifold with the prescribed image.

label: The Exact Sequence
notes: The construction is governed by a short exact sequence. The map pi is onto and carries the integer lattice onto the integer lattice, precisely the Delzant smoothness condition. Its kernel n is the Lie algebra of the subtorus we reduce by; the dual sequence supplies the projection used to restrict the standard moment map of C to the d.

label: Interval to CP^1
notes: Run the smallest case. The interval from zero to a has two normals, minus one and plus one, so pi from R two to R has kernel the diagonal line. The subtorus is the diagonal circle in the two-torus, the zero level is a sphere of radius root two a in C squared, and quotienting by that circle yields complex projective one.

label: A Dictionary of Examples
notes: Collect the dictionary. The standard n-simplex labels complex projective n-space, a unit square labels the product of two projective lines, and shearing or truncating that square produces the Hirzebruch surfaces. Reading off vertices, edges, and lattice lengths recovers fixed points, invariant spheres, and symplectic areas directly from the picture.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: To recap, symplectic toric manifolds are classified by Delzant polytopes through the moment image: simple, rational, smooth, up to translation. The primitive normals bridge polytope and torus through an exact sequence, and reduction realizes any Delzant polytope. Next lecture fleshes out the construction and proves it returns the polytope we started from.
